decisions.reason: The placement constraint does not change the three-board architecture or the assigned roles of the main and sensor boards.

The local context applies the downward-facing edge constraint to the vertically mounted main and sensor boards; it does not change the power-board form factor or its existing back-side battery connector.
Minimizing placement on a downward-facing side does not alter the power board's four-layer stack.

The source adds a connector-placement constraint owned by the source Requirement; it does not resolve or modify the separate finding that the specified main-board contents cannot fit within the given dimensions.
The charge-status indication path, connector, resistor, and LED population requirements remain unchanged; the source does not identify any required relocation of this interface.
The source constrains physical placement generally but does not change the reset connector's electrical action, panel mounting, or connector-based implementation.
Connector placement is represented by the source Requirement; the signal connector types, references, and pinouts remain valid unchanged.
The bottom-side placement constraint does not change the sensor board's connector inventory, references, pinouts, or hub role.
The source affects physical connector placement, not the interboard power topology, connector specifications, or pin-order rule.

This Requirement concerns bottom-side pin labels on the power board, while the supplied context concerns placement on the vertically mounted main and sensor boards and does not remove or relocate the labels.
The source does not change the power-button connector's board assignment, signal connection, mounting, or switch behavior.
The general placement constraint does not change the GPIO assignments, connector identities, or off-board panel-control behavior.
